proposals.prompt:
Agents in a supermarket gridworld must collect their required items and leave through the exit. Every action costs the same, so demonstrators prefer short trajectories -- unless an unknown social norm makes them behave otherwise. Your task is to propose candidate norms (obligations or prohibitions) that could explain the demonstrated behaviour.
Each demonstration is listed step by step as  `k: {atoms true in the state} action`.

Available atoms:
- at(x,y) -- the agent is at cell (x,y); x = column (0 = left), y = row (0 = top); N decreases y, S increases y, E increases x, W decreases x
- actions N, S, E, W, MOVE (any of the four moves), INTERACT (any interaction with an object: the different kinds of interaction are NOT distinguished), EXIT (leave the store; always the last action)

Propose norms using ONLY the atoms listed above. Do NOT define any new state properties or events: "abstraction" must be {}.
Propose 8 diverse candidate hypotheses.

Output format: return ONLY a JSON list (no prose, no code fences). Each element:
{"id": short_name, "text": one-sentence natural-language statement of the norm,
 "abstraction": {"state_properties": {name: FORMULA, ...},
                 "events": {name: {"pre": FORMULA, "post": FORMULA or null}, ...}},
 "norm": {"type": "prohibition", "condition": FORMULA}
       | {"type": "obligation", "trigger": FORMULA or "START", "discharge": FORMULA}}
FORMULA := atom | name of a property/event defined in this hypothesis | {"not": F} | {"and": [F, ...]}
         | {"or": [F, ...]} | {"le"|"lt"|"ge"|"gt"|"eq": [numeric_feature, integer]}
Semantics.  A trajectory is a sequence of steps (state s_k, action a_k).  A step's label contains the atoms true in
s_k and the action a_k.  A state property is a formula over state atoms (no actions).  An event
{"pre": P, "post": Q} occurs at step k when P holds for the label of step k and Q holds in the next state s_{k+1}
(post may be null).  A prohibition counts one violation for every step whose label (including events occurring at
that step) satisfies the condition.  An obligation becomes pending at any step satisfying the trigger ("START" =
pending from the beginning) and is fulfilled by a later (or the same) step satisfying the discharge; it can be
triggered again; it is violated if it is still pending when the trajectory ends.

Semantics.  A trajectory is a sequence of steps (state s_k, action a_k).  A step's label contains the atoms true in
s_k and the action a_k.  A state property is a formula over state atoms (no actions).  An event
{"pre": P, "post": Q} occurs at step k when P holds for the label of step k and Q holds in the next state s_{k+1}
(post may be null).  A prohibition counts one violation for every step whose label (including events occurring at
that step) satisfies the condition.  An obligation becomes pending at any step satisfying the trigger ("START" =
pending from the beginning) and is fulfilled by a later (or the same) step satisfying the discharge; it can be
triggered again; it is violated if it is still pending when the trajectory ends.

parsed.text: A shopper is obliged to take the entrance cart before doing the shopping trip.
A shopper is prohibited from picking up shelf items unless they currently have the cart.
A shopper is prohibited from carrying groceries by hand rather than using the cart.
After taking possession of a cart, the shopper is obliged to return it to the top-left cart bay.
A shopper is prohibited from leaving the cart anywhere except the designated top-left return bay.
A shopper is prohibited from exiting unless the cart has been parked at the designated return bay.
A shopper may leave the top-left bay to the east only after dropping the cart; pushing the cart east from that bay is prohibited.
The final approach to the exit is a cart-free zone, so shoppers are prohibited from entering it while still holding the cart.

accepted.description: [g1_must_take_cart_at_entrance] OBLIGED: after start, eventually take_entrance_cart (before exit)  where entrance_cart_station := (at(1,5) ∧ cartAt(1,5)); take_entrance_cart := (entrance_cart_station ∧ PICKUP_CART) · hasCart
[g1_no_item_pickup_without_cart] FORBIDDEN: uncarted_item_pickup  where without_cart := ¬hasCart; uncarted_item_pickup := (without_cart ∧ PICKUP_ITEM)

[g1_cart_must_be_returned_to_bay] OBLIGED: after hasCart, eventually return_cart_to_bay (before exit)  where cart_parked_at_return_bay := cartAt(0,1); cart_return_bay := at(0,1); return_cart_to_bay := (cart_return_bay ∧ hasCart ∧ LEAVE_CART) · cart_parked_at_return_bay

[g1_no_abandon_cart_elsewhere] FORBIDDEN: leave_cart_outside_bay  where at_cart_return_bay := at(0,1); not_at_cart_return_bay := ¬at_cart_return_bay; leave_cart_outside_bay := (LEAVE_CART ∧ not_at_cart_return_bay)
[g1_no_exit_with_unreturned_cart] FORBIDDEN: (EXIT ∧ cart_not_parked_at_return_bay)  where cart_not_parked_at_return_bay := ¬cart_parked_at_return_bay; cart_parked_at_return_bay := cartAt(0,1)
[g1_no_east_from_return_bay_with_cart] FORBIDDEN: (pushing_cart_at_return_bay ∧ E)  where at_cart_return_bay := at(0,1); pushing_cart_at_return_bay := (at_cart_return_bay ∧ hasCart)

[g1_no_cart_in_exit_approach] FORBIDDEN: cart_in_exit_approach_zone  where cart_in_exit_approach_zone := (exit_approach_zone ∧ hasCart); exit_approach_zone := (at(7,2) ∨ at(8,2) ∨ at(9,2) ∨ at(7,3) ∨ at(8,3) ∨ at(9,3) ∨ at(9,4) ∨ at(9,5))
